Replication values are author-derived primary project-table entries; no metric conversion performed. N (R) is retained as named, with exclusions unknown. Primary table URL https://osf.io/3h29d/; assigned locator https://osf.io/3h29d.
Source follow-up: Fresh original-only extraction from supplied published article. Title, authors and numerical meanings visually verified on rendered PDF pp. 1, 3 and 4. Source PDF: /home/lukas/work/fred-mac-recovery-20261030/continuation-1201/private_batch_02/artifacts/66028bad248522889a8ffb73_ebsco.pdf. Canonical text glyphs are preserved in quotations: text 5 means the printed equals sign, and Zp 2 ¼ :045 represents printed partial eta-squared = .045. The printed .92 is p_rep, not a conventional p value; conventional p is not printed for this test, so p.value and p.bound remain null, with confident=true denoting verified absence for the selected test. No conversion performed. The four-group attraction-effect hypothesis is tested by the explicitly identified focused interaction contrast. The separately reported omnibus eight-cell ANOVA is F(7, 112) = 3.67, partial eta-squared .187, p_rep .99; these are different-test statistics and were not merged. Analytic n=120 is established by the stated enrollment and lost record and the Table 1 counts, rather than printed as a standalone total; the focused contrast nevertheless prints denominator df 111, retained without correction. No manuscript or embedded appendix was used. Replication and narrative replication success are unassigned placeholders.
